sections.title: What an MT5 White Label Actually Means

blocks.text: There's a fair bit of confusion around this term, so let's keep it simple.

MT5 runs on a server operated under a licence from the platform developer. With a full licence, you own and run that server yourself. That gives you the most control, but it also comes with a large upfront cost and a lot of technical responsibility.

With a white label, your brokerage operates within an existing licensed MT5 environment. You get your own branded setup, your own client groups and manager access to run your business day to day. The core server sits under the licence holder's arrangement rather than yours.
For most new brokers, that trade-off makes sense. Lower startup costs, faster time to market, and you can always look at moving to a full deployment later as volumes grow.
One important point. A white label is a technology arrangement. It isn't a financial licence and it doesn't give you permission to offer trading services anywhere. That part is covered further down.
A white label MT5 setup tends to work well for:
* New brokers who want to launch on MT5 without committing to a full server licence on day one
* Introducing brokers ready to move clients under their own brand
* Regional brokerages testing a new market before investing in bigger infrastructure
* Businesses currently on MT4 who want to move to MT5 without a heavy upfront spend

If you already process high volumes, need deep control over server-level settings or plan to run several entities from one environment, a full deployment might suit you better. We're happy to talk through both.
01 Requirements
We start with your business model. Which markets, which instruments, which account types, which liquidity provider. These answers shape every configuration decision that follows.
02 Environment Setup
Your white label environment is created and branded, with server access and hosting arranged.
03 Configuration

Groups, symbols, trading conditions and manager permissions get configured. This step takes care, because small mistakes here, like a wrong contract size or margin setting, can turn into real money problems later.
04 Connectivity and Integrations
Liquidity is connected, and your CRM, KYC and payment providers are linked to MT5.
05 Testing
We test pricing, execution, rejects, margin calls, stop outs, swaps and commissions, along with the full client journey from sign-up to first trade. Your team joins in to check its own workflows.
06 Launch and Ongoing Support
Go-live with monitoring in place. After that, we handle configuration changes, new symbols, new account types and day-to-day technical issues as your brokerage grows.

What's Included
Branding and Platform Setup

Your brokerage name and branding applied where the white label arrangement allows it, including desktop, web and mobile terminal access for your clients. We also set up the company details clients see when they log in.
Trading Groups and Account Types
We create the groups behind each account type you want to offer. Standard, raw spread, swap-free, demo, IB-linked accounts. Each one gets its own leverage, margin, commission and swap settings.
Symbols and Trading Conditions

Forex pairs, metals, indices, energies, whatever your liquidity supports and your business model calls for. We configure contract sizes, trading hours, spreads, markups, stop levels and margin requirements symbol by symbol.
Manager and Admin Access
Your dealing, risk and support teams get role-based access, so each person sees and changes only what they're meant to.
Hosting and Server Setup
Depending on the arrangement, we either deploy and host the relevant server components or coordinate with the environment your white label sits in. Either way, monitoring and backups are part of it.
Liquidity Connectivity
We connect your groups to your liquidity provider through a bridge, an MT5 gateway or FIX, and set up symbol mapping and routing rules to match your execution model.
CRM, KYC and Payment Integration
New clients register, verify and fund their accounts through your CRM, with trading accounts created automatically on MT5. No manual account creation, no spreadsheets in between.
Testing, Launch and Support
Full testing before go-live, close monitoring after it, and ongoing technical support once you're running.

Use Cases
A New Brokerage Going Live

A startup brokerage wants to be on MT5 within a sensible budget. A white label gives them branded terminals, their own account types and liquidity connectivity without the cost of a full licence. They put the savings into marketing and compliance instead.
An IB Becoming a Broker

An introducing broker has been sending clients to another brokerage for years. With a white label, they launch under their own brand, keep the relationship with their clients and build revenue that's actually theirs.
An MT4 Broker Moving to MT5

A broker on MT4 wants MT5's broader instrument range and newer features but isn't ready for a full server licence. A white label lets them move across in stages, running both platforms side by side during the transition.

fullBlocks.text: Licensing and Responsibilities
This needs saying plainly. An MT5 white label is a technology service. It doesn't give you a financial licence, regulatory approval or permission to offer trading in any jurisdiction.
What We Handle
White label setup, branding, platform configuration, hosting arrangements, liquidity connectivity, CRM, KYC and payment integrations, testing and ongoing technical support.
What Stays With You
Company formation, financial licensing, regulatory compliance, client agreements, risk disclosures, liquidity and payment provider contracts, and how you market your services.
Third Parties

The MT5 platform is developed by a third party, and the white label environment operates under a licence arrangement with them. We aren't affiliated with or endorsed by the platform developer unless clearly stated. Liquidity providers, KYC services and payment providers each have their own terms, which sit between you and them directly.
Rules on offering trading services vary by jurisdiction, so speak with qualified legal and regulatory advisors in your target markets.
Frequently Asked Questions
What's the difference between an MT5 white label and a full licence?

With a full licence, you own and run your own MT5 server, which means higher costs and more control. With a white label, you operate inside an existing licensed environment under your own brand. It's cheaper and quicker to launch, with somewhat less server-level control.
fullBlocks.parentH3: What's the difference between an MT5 white label and a full licence?

fullBlocks.text: How is a white label different from a grey label?

The terms get used loosely across the industry. Generally, a white label gives you more branding and configuration control, while a grey label sits more directly under another provider's infrastructure and arrangement. We'll explain exactly what you get with any setup before you commit.
fullBlocks.parentH3: How is a white label different from a grey label?

fullBlocks.text: Will my clients see my brand or someone else's?
Your clients interact with your brand through the terminals, client portal and communications. What's visible depends on the specific arrangement, and we'll go through that clearly during scoping.
fullBlocks.parentH3: Will my clients see my brand or someone else's?

fullBlocks.text: Can I set my own spreads, leverage and account types?
Yes, within the limits of your liquidity setup and the rules that apply in your jurisdiction. You can run several account types with different conditions.
fullBlocks.parentH3: Can I set my own spreads, leverage and account types?

fullBlocks.text: Can I connect my own liquidity provider?
Usually, yes. We connect your chosen provider through a bridge, gateway or FIX, depending on what they support.
fullBlocks.parentH3: Can I connect my own liquidity provider?

fullBlocks.text: How long does an MT5 broker setup take with a white label?

It depends on your account structure, the number of integrations and how quickly your third-party providers respond. White labels generally launch faster than full deployments. We'll give you a realistic timeline after scoping.
fullBlocks.parentH3: How long does an MT5 broker setup take with a white label?

fullBlocks.text: Can I move from a white label to a full MT5 server later?
Yes. Many brokers start on a white label and move to their own server as they grow. We plan the configuration so that migration, when it comes, is as straightforward as possible.
fullBlocks.parentH3: Can I move from a white label to a full MT5 server later?

fullBlocks.text: Does a white label include a licence to operate as a broker?
No. An MT5 white label covers the technology only. Financial licensing and regulatory approval are separate, and they remain your responsibility.
fullBlocks.parentH3: Does a white label include a licence to operate as a broker?
